text:
emma-support: Hi team, Nexus customer NexGen Analytics is reporting objects that should have been deleted per their custom retention (90d) are still returning in searches and via the object GET API. They filed a support ticket and want an ETA. Escalating to eng/security.
olivia-support: Customer says they set custom_retention=90d on 2026-09-01, and objects created 2026-04-01 are expected to be gone by now. They provided sample IDs: obj_9a1b2c3d, obj_4f5e6d7c.
sam-sre: Noted. Any errors when we attempted to delete? Logs?
maria-privacy: Also flagging potential compliance impact. If deletes didn't run, legal needs to be looped. Do we have audit entries for delete requests?
jon-platops: I pulled the deletion job logs for the retention worker namespace. I see the scheduler queued deletions on 2026-09-02, but the worker returned 500 when calling the storage delete API for a subset of keys. Example log snippet:
```
2026-09-02T03:12:07Z WARN retention-worker delete_failed key=obj_9a1b2c3d error="storage: 500 InternalServerError - kms: encryption_key_unavailable"
```
kendra-eng-runtime: That suggests the storage layer couldn't decrypt due to a KMS issue. We had a KMS key rotation in prod around 2026-09-01 (rolling), maybe some hosts pointed to old key material during TTL purge window.
dave-kms: We rotated key rk-main-prod on 2026-09-01 02:00 UTC. HSM logs show a few hosts had transient UNAVAILABLE responses during rotation window for ~7m. We retried, most succeeded. I will check if those object encryption key IDs map to keys that were rotated.
olivia-support: The customer also says the DELETE API returns 500 when they call it manually: "HTTP 500 InternalServerError - unable to decrypt object key".
jon-platops: Can you repro locally with the sample ID? I ran `curl -X DELETE https://api.redwood.com/v1/objects/obj_9a1b2c3d` (internal call) and saw the same 500. Stack trace points at storage.adapter.Delete -> kms.DecryptKey failing.
emma-support: Customer wants immediate remediation and confirmation that objects are fully purged within 24 hours.
sam-sre: Short term: we can re-run the retention purge for affected object IDs with a KMS fallback path. Plan: 1) Identify affected object key IDs (jon), 2) Request KMS team to re-expose old key material or perform a one-time forced-unwrap for those key IDs (dave), 3) Re-run delete job and validate audit entries and search index removal (kendra).
maria-privacy: Legal requests we preserve an immutable copy of current state and note all actions for the audit trail before doing destructive ops. Also need to capture customer consent for any forced unwrap.
dave-kms: I can run a targeted unwrap attempt. If key material is gone (rotated+destroyed) we need to leverage key-escrow or key-recovery policy — that takes longer. I'll triage now and post status within 30m.
jon-platops: I've started a job to list objects with failed deletion status between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-05. Attaching snippet of query we ran:
```
SELECT object_id FROM retention_audit
WHERE status = 'delete_failed' AND time_window >= '2026-09-01' AND reason LIKE '%kms%';
```
Results: ~42 objects across NexGen's tenant, incl the two sample IDs.
kendra-eng-runtime: After successful delete we must ensure the search index and metadata store mark deleted=true and the audit log contains: `actor=system retention-run reason=kms_unwrap_retry outcome=success`.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-4293 - retention-purge-failure-NexGen (severity=P2) assigned to sam-sre, jon-platops, dave-kms.
olivia-support: Customer is asking if this is a billing/usage issue — they saw no access charges but are worried about data exposure. Can we confirm whether objects were readable while the worker failed?
sam-sre: Based on access logs, there were no public GETs for those object IDs after 2026-09-02. However, internal replicas might have served stale index results. Search system may show them until index reconciliation.
emma-support: Next steps and owners: dave-kms (investigate unwrap + HSM logs, ETA 30m); jon-platops (identify full object set and re-run delete job, ETA 1h after unwrap success); kendra (validate index purge + audit entries, ETA 2h after delete run); maria-privacy (prepare compliance memo and obtain customer's written consent for forced unwrap, ETA 1h). I'll keep customer updated.
dave-kms: Quick update: HSM shows two UNAVAILABLE windows at 02:00 and 02:07 UTC, but keys were not destroyed. I can perform targeted re-unwraps for the 42 object key IDs. Starting now.
jon-platops: I'm packaging the object list and kicking off the re-run once dave confirms re-unwraps. Script below to re-run retention purge for list `nexgen_failed_ids.txt`:
```
cat nexgen_failed_ids.txt | xargs -n1 -P10 curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/retry_delete -d @-
```
kendra-eng-runtime: If the re-run returns 200 for delete, we should wait 5 minutes and then call `search.invalidate(object_id)` for each ID, then check `metadata_store.get(object_id)` returns 404.
maria-privacy: I've drafted a short consent template for NexGen to sign allowing KMS key unwrap for these specific objects and to acknowledge remediation steps. Sending to olivia to forward.
olivia-support: Sent to customer and they replied ok by email — "we consent to expedited remediation for the listed object IDs." Forwarded to this thread.
dave-kms: Completed targeted unwraps for 42 keys. Returning success for all — no need for key-recovery.
jon-platops: Re-run started. Progress: 42/42 delete retries returned 200 OK within the last 8 minutes.
kendra-eng-runtime: Index invalidation done. Metadata checks: obj_9a1b2c3d -> 404, obj_4f5e6d7c -> 404. Audit entries created with actor=system retention_retry outcome=success. I'm pushing a summary to the audit-s3 folder now.
emma-support: Great. Olivia, please confirm with customer and close ticket once they acknowledge. Maria, please save compliance memo in case legal needs it.
maria-privacy: Memo saved in compliance drive with incident ID INC-2026-4293. Also flagged for quarterly retention review — suggested adding a pre-rotation retention-check for future KMS rotations.
sam-sre: Postmortem items: 1) Add KMS rotation check to retention-worker (skip deletion if KMS in rotating state), 2) Add stronger retry/backoff and queue for failures, 3) Alerting if deletion fail rate > 0.1% for a tenant in a 24h window.
emma-support: Customer update message: "We've completed an expedited remediation run; 42 objects removed and audit logs show successful deletes. Sorry for the disruption — we're adding safeguards to reduce recurrence. Please let us know if you see anything else." Olivia, send.
olivia-support: Sent. Customer acknowledged and closed their case at 2026-09-03T11:45:00Z. Marking this thread resolved.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: #INC-2026-4293 - retention-purge-failure-NexGen (resolved by sam-sre, jon-platops, dave-kms)
